name: Supernumerary Kidney

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Radiologic and Anatomical Diagnostic Criteria for Supernumerary Kidney

criteria.description: Presence of a distinct kidney with its own capsule separate from the ipsilateral kidney
Independent arterial and venous supply to the supernumerary kidney
Separate ureter draining the supernumerary kidney, either joining the ipsilateral ureter or draining independently
Identification of the supernumerary kidney on imaging modalities such as ultrasound, CT, or MRI

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of a distinct kidney with separate capsule and independent vascular supply confirmed by imaging
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily radiological and anatomical; histopathology is rarely required.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Palpable abdominal or flank mass corresponding to accessory kidney
searchTerms: felt lump in abdomen or side

pathognomonic.symptomName: Imaging evidence of an additional renal parenchymal structure

common.notes: Due to abnormal drainage or stasis

common.symptomName: Flank pain localized to the side of the supernumerary kidney

searchTerms: swelling of extra kidney due to urine buildup

occasional.symptomName: Hypertension secondary to renin secretion abnormalities

rare.symptomName: Renal calculi formation in the supernumerary kidney
Infection leading to pyelonephritis of the accessory kidney
Malignant transformation within the supernumerary kidney

laboratory: Urinalysis may show hematuria or pyuria
Elevated inflammatory markers if infection present
imaging: Ultrasound demonstrating additional renal tissue with separate capsule
CT or MRI showing distinct renal parenchyma with independent vascular supply
Intravenous urography revealing separate ureteral drainage
genetic: No specific genetic mutations identified; sporadic congenital anomaly
other: Surgical exploration may confirm diagnosis if imaging inconclusive

distinguishingFeatures: Duplicated collecting system without separate renal parenchyma
Multiple cysts within a single kidney
No separate vascular supply or ureter

redFlags: Sudden onset of severe flank pain indicating obstruction or infection
Signs of sepsis in urinary tract infection
references: Saxena AK, et al. Supernumerary kidney: a rare congenital anomaly. Indian J Urol. 2010.
Campbell-Walsh Urology, 12th Edition, Chapter on Congenital Anomalies of the Kidney and Urinary Tract.
